title: Ἀνὴρ κακοπράγμων
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 50 (= Perry 36). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἀνὴρ κακοπράγμων συνορισάμενος πρός τινα ψευδὲς ἐπιδείξειν τὸ ἐν Δελφοῖς μαντεῖον, ὡς ἐνέστη ἡ προθεσμία, λαβὼν στρουθίον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα καὶ τοῦτο τῷ ἱματίῳ σκεπάσας, ἧκεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ στὰς ἀντικρὺς ἐπηρώτα πότερόν τι ἔμπνουν ἔχει μετὰ χεῖρας ἢ ἄψυχον, βουλόμενος, ἐὰν μὲν ἄψυχον εἴπῃ, ζωὸν τὸ στρουθίον ἐπιδεῖξαι, ἐὰν δὲ ἔμπνουν, ἀποπνίξας προενεγκεῖν.
sentences.tr: Anēr kakopragmōn synorisamenos pros tina pseudes epideixein to en Delphois manteion, hōs enestē hē prothesmia, labōn strouthion eis tēn cheira kai touto tōi himatiōi skepasas, hēken eis to hieron kai stas antikrys epērōta poteron ti empnoun echei meta cheiras ē apsychon, boulomenos, ean men apsychon eipēi, zōon to strouthion epideixai, ean de empnoun, apopnixas proenenkein.
sentences.l: A mischief-making man, having made a compact with someone that he would show the oracle at Delphi false, when the appointed day came on, having taken a small bird into his hand and having covered it with his cloak, came to the temple and, having stood right opposite, asked whether he had something breathing in his hands or something lifeless — wishing, if it should say 'lifeless', to show the bird alive, but if 'breathing', to throttle it and bring it out.
sentences.i: A dishonest fellow made an agreement with someone that he would prove the oracle at Delphi false. When the appointed day came, he took a small bird in his hand, covered it with his cloak, went to the temple, and standing directly before it asked whether what he held in his hands was breathing or lifeless — meaning, if the answer was 'lifeless', to show the bird alive, and if 'breathing', to strangle it and bring it out.
sentences.n: συνορισάμενος is a rare verb; the sense taken here, 'having come to terms, having made an agreement', is the best that can be got from it. The rest of the sentence is a chain of aorist participles — λαβών, σκεπάσας, στάς, ἀποπνίξας — each one a step taken before the main verb. This chain is the engine of Aesopic narrative and will be met in nearly every fable. πότερον … ἤ frames a double question, 'whether … or'. ἐάν with the subjunctive (εἴπῃ) inside βουλόμενος keeps his calculation in the form he made it. Delphi was Apollo's oracle, the most authoritative in the Greek world; catching it out is the whole point of the undertaking.

sentences.t: Καὶ ὁ θεὸς συνεὶς αὐτοῦ τὴν κακότεχνον γνώμην εἶπεν· « Ἀλλ’ ὦ οὗτος, πέπαυσο· ἐν σοὶ γάρ ἐστι τοῦτο ὃ ἔχεις ἢ νεκρὸν εἶναι ἢ ἔμψυχον. »
sentences.tr: Kai ho theos syneis autou tēn kakotechnon gnōmēn eipen· « All' ō houtos, pepauso· en soi gar esti touto ho echeis ē nekron einai ē empsychon. »
sentences.l: And the god, having understood his crafty intention, said: « But, you there, stop: for it lies in you for this which you hold to be either dead or alive. »
sentences.i: And the god, seeing through his malicious design, said: « You there — have done. It rests with you whether the thing you hold is dead or alive. »
sentences.n: πέπαυσο is a perfect imperative, more peremptory than the present would be: stop, and be stopped. ὦ οὗτος, 'you there', is brusque address, never polite. ἐν σοί ἐστι, 'it is in you', is the ordinary idiom for 'it is up to you', and what is up to him is put as an infinitive, εἶναι.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι τὸ θεῖον ἀπαρεγχείρητόν ἐστι.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti to theion aparencheirēton esti.
sentences.l: The story shows that the divine is not to be tampered with.
sentences.n: ἀπαρεγχείρητον is a rare word, built on παρεγχειρέω 'lay a hand on, meddle with' — 'not open to meddling'. The neuter τὸ θεῖον, 'the divine', is the usual Greek way of speaking of godhead in the abstract.
